title: Shadow-sink differential detector + soft-rollback policy for function-call surface changes
creator: Asha Patel
description:
Summary:

Implement a shadow-sink differential detector that continuously compares function-call / tool-invocation surfaces between a candidate model variant and the current serving model, and a conservative soft-rollback policy that can automatically ramp down or revert a rollout when unsafe diffs are detected. The goal is to reduce silent breakages (unexpected tool-call schema changes, parameter renames, or argument-type swaps) during canary/A-B/shadow experiments while keeping rollback behavior predictable and auditable.

Design goals and constraints:
- Non-invasive: collector runs as a passive shadow pipeline (no traffic mutation) and attaches per-invocation metadata to existing tracing logs.
- Low noise: heuristics should avoid frequent false positives from benign formatting changes (e.g., key ordering, extra metadata fields).
- Actionable signals: provide both coarse signals (overall function-call count delta) and fine-grained signals (per-function argument-name/shape diffs, missing/extra required fields).
- Gradual automation: support 3 escalation tiers — notify, pause ramp, auto-soft-rollback — configurable per-customer/project.
- Privacy/compliance: shadow payloads must obey PII redaction rules and customer opt-outs (follow Private deployment KMS/audit controls).

Detection approach (high-level):
1) Shadow-sink capture: routing rules duplicate a percentage of incoming requests to the candidate variant, record the candidate's function-call list and the baseline model's function-call list in the shadow sink. Each record includes function name, ordered argument names, argument types (inferred: string, number, list, object), argument presence/absence, and a stable fingerprint (sha256 of normalized shape).

2) Structural diffing: for each invocation pair, compute:
   - Signature delta: function names invoked by candidate but not baseline and vice versa (counts and unique set).
   - Argument presence diff: fields newly missing/added, with frequency over a sliding 1h and 24h window.
   - Shape drift score: fraction of arguments with changed inferred type or changed nested shape beyond X complexity threshold.

3) Aggregation and scoring: produce per-function metrics and cluster-level summaries. Score is a weighted sum of:
   - new_fn_rate (weight 0.4)
   - missing_required_arg_rate (weight 0.3)
   - shape_drift_rate (weight 0.2)
   - downstream-error-coupling (weight 0.1): correlation with downstream tool failures or non-200s.
Default thresholds (initial proposal):
   - warn when score > 0.07 (i.e., small but notable drift)
   - pause ramp when score > 0.2 OR missing_required_arg_rate > 5%
   - auto-soft-rollback when score > 0.35 AND downstream-error-coupling > 10%
These defaults can be tuned per-customer/route.

Soft-rollback policy (behavior):
- Soft-rollback = deterministic traffic ramp down strategy: shrink candidate weight by 50% immediately, pause any scheduled increases, and create an incident/ticket with attached evidence. If score persists above auto-rollback threshold after a configurable wait window (default 10 minutes of stable signal), perform a full reversion to previous model for that route.
- Audit trail: every automated action emits an immutable event (who/what/why) linked to the rollout record in Console.
- Manual override: SRE/PM/owner can mark a diff as acceptable for a rollout (allowlist signatures) to suppress future alerts for same pattern. Allowlist changes must go through audit log and require a review.

Telemetry and observability:
- New metrics: candidate_fn_set_delta, per_fn_missing_arg_pct, per_fn_shape_drift_score, shadow_false_positive_rate (estimated via sampling), rollback_trigger_count.
- Dashboards: per-route widget showing rolling histograms of signature deltas and a timeline of ramp adjustments + events.
- Alerting: multi-window alert (1m, 10m, 1h) with severity mapping to the escalation tiers.

Evaluation plan / test harness:
- Offline replay: use captured historical traffic to simulate candidate variants with injected diffs (rename arg, drop arg, change type). Measure detection sensitivity and false positive rate. Target sensitivity >90% for missing required args and false positive rate <3% on benign formatting changes.
- Shadow-only controlled rollout: enable shadow sink at 1% sampling for internal customers for 2 weeks, iterate thresholds based on observed drift distribution.
- Canary integration: wire detection signals into canary engine for canary weights of 5%, 25%, 50% with automatic hold/rollback triggers.

Data retention and privacy:
- Shadow payloads stored encrypted; PII redaction applied before long-term storage. Short-term (7d) unredacted buffer for investigation, long-term only shape/metrics. Reflects Private deployment audit controls.

API/UX changes required:
- Console: new rollout view tab "Function-call safety" with per-function diffs, allowlist buttons, and "start soft-rollback" control.
- SDK/API: rollout create/update endpoints accept a new safety_policy block (escalation tier, thresholds, sample_rate, allowlist).

Trade-offs discussed:
- Aggressiveness vs noise: lower thresholds catch regressions earlier but increase ops noise. Decision: start conservative, iterate based on shadow rollout telemetry.
- Complexity of shape matching: full deep structural equality is expensive; use normalized fingerprinting + lightweight type inference. Will revisit for heavy nested payload use-cases.

Open questions / next steps:
- Determine default required-arg list per function (some functions are intentionally flexible). Proposal: infer required-ness from baseline model: fields present in >95% of baseline invocations considered required unless annotated otherwise.
- Confirm retention window for unredacted shadow traces with security/compliance.
- Run the offline replay job and produce an initial ROC curve by 2025-11-12 (owner: Marcus).
